title: Oil Reserves Dangerously Low; ‘Much Higher’ Fuel Prices By Winter | Josh Young
speaker: Josh Young (Bison Interests)

macro_themes.view: Reported near-normal tanker traffic is convoy surges and propaganda; sustained crude flows are well below pre-war, with ~5% of tankers hit.
Diesel/gasoline at ~$200-250/bbl equivalent is extreme; counter-seasonal refinery runs and Europe's diesel release should rebuild product stocks and compress cracks.
Refiners turning crude into products plus low SPR releases (SPR lowest since 1982) should drain crude stocks and lift crude prices into winter.
Net speculative crude positioning is near record lows relative to price, historically a setup for much higher prices.
Gives very low weight to claims the Iran war ends soon.

calls.reason: Elevated refinery runs will draw down already-low crude inventories while Hormuz flows stay impaired; bearish positioning is a contrarian bullish signal. Sees the 32% odds of $115+ WTI by year-end as closer to his view.
calls.quote: I've been bullish oil for a while and um I think I think this could be the trigger for much much higher prices.

calls.reason: Product prices at unsustainably high levels; counter-seasonal refining, Europe's diesel release and possibly fewer strikes on Russian refineries should lower diesel and crack spreads.
calls.quote: I do think that you'll see these refined product margins fall a lot just because they are at unsustainably high levels.

notes: Host states 'Monday, October 5th'. HO used for diesel/refining-margin view (not in the canonical list; group rates_fx_energy). WTI 'just below $90' quoted by host. No specific stock picks.
